report.source_text: Post-mortem analysis confirmed these findings. Although partially necrotic, the renal mass and extensive metastases involving the retroperitoneum, thorax, and abdominal cavity were noted to have tumor cells with clear cytoplasm. The renal and lung blocks were positive for EMA and CA-IX. A cytology sample from his 4R lymph node biopsy was also reviewed at this time, from which lesional cells were positive for CA-IX and PAX8, with retained expression of FH and SDHB (Fig. 2). These results were most consistent with mccRCC with rhabdoid differentiation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: post-mortem diagnosis of metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (mccRCC)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man presented with cough, shortness of breath, and signs consistent with embolic phenomena including left leg swelling and purple toes. Initial labs showed systemic illness features. Imaging revealed a 4.7 cm right renal mass with enlarged retroperitoneal, mesenteric, and thoracic lymph nodes consistent with metastases. Thoracentesis showed atypical epithelioid cells. Over 3 weeks, the renal mass grew to 6 cm with enlarging metastases. Ante-mortem lymph node biopsy showed atypical immunophenotype suggestive of epithelioid angiomyolipoma but clinical context favored metastatic RCC. The patient clinically declined and died one month after diagnosis. Post-mortem examination confirmed metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma with rhabdoid differentiation, supported by positive immunohistochemical markers (EMA, CA-IX, PAX8) and retained FH and SDHB expression.
